title: Primary versus post-primary (adult-type) TB
dek: Primary disease is the Ghon-complex chapter: first-infection pneumonia, nodes, possible miliary seed. Post-primary (adult-type) disease is apical cavitation and the airborne engine. They are chapters, not two species.
story: Primary tuberculosis is the first-infection sequence: droplet nucleus to mid-zone or lower-zone pneumonitis, draining nodes, a Ghon focus that may calcify as a Ranke complex. In immunologically naive hosts — young children, HIV with low CD4 — this chapter can progress (primary progressive disease, miliary, meningeal) instead of quieting.

Post-primary, also called adult-type or “secondary” TB, is the apical-posterior cavitary pattern that dominates infectious smear-positive disease in immunocompetent adolescents and adults. It can follow remote primary infection (reactivation) or reinfection. The radiology and the aerosol output are the point, not a moral about who was “careless.”

The Ghon glossary plate owns the eponym. This plate is the chapter split so that “primary” is not used as a synonym for “pediatric” or for “smear-negative,” and so that an upper-lobe cavity is not called a Ghon focus.
deepTitle: What the split changes in practice
deep: Infectiousness: cavitary post-primary disease is the classic high-output source. Primary nodes in a toddler are usually not the engine; the adult source is.
IGRA/TST: both chapters can be IGRA-positive. The test does not name the chapter.
HIV: low CD4 blurs the adult-type pattern toward primary-progressive and disseminated disease. Smear can be negative with high burden.
Genomics: relapse versus reinfection is a strain fork, not a synonym for post-primary versus primary. An adult cavity can be reinfection.

example.title: Upper-lobe cavity labelled “Ghon”
example.setup: A 28-year-old, smear 3+, right apical cavity. The radiology report says “Ghon complex.” Contact investigation is deprioritised because “primary TB in adults is not infectious.”

steps.title: Wrong eponym
steps.body: An apical cavity is adult-type / post-primary disease until proven otherwise. Ghon is a primary-focus word, usually mid-zone plus node.

steps.title: Infectiousness follows anatomy
steps.body: This is the droplet-nucleus engine. Infection control and contacts are urgent. Pediatric primary nodes would have pointed you at an adult source, not away from isolation.

steps.title: Strain story is separate
steps.body: Whether this cavity is reactivation or reinfection is a WGS question against any old isolate, not a caption on the CXR.

example.takeaway: Primary is the first-infection chapter. Cavities are the adult-type engine. Do not mix eponyms.

check.answer: The primary-infection complex (often with a node as Ranke)
check.why: Ghon is a primary-chapter eponym. Cavities are a different layer on the plate.
